verticalReference.evidence: OS local correction TQ3883/TQ3983 and 2003 crest comparison. Historic Liverpool attribution and benchmark identity remain conditional; this is not a survey calibration.

method: Piecewise linear triangulation of ground and street observations, excluding every triangle touching mapped water or reviewed canal/structure exclusions, or with an edge longer than 500 m. No extrapolation, modern terrain fill, bank heights or benchmark offsets.
streetPolicy: Street dots anchor the contemporary developed surface at their measured levels. Marsh lanes may constrain neighbouring ground approximately where better evidence is absent. Treat lane-to-marsh relief as an uncertain local difference, not a reason to discard the lane level. No automatic fill subtraction or large fill assumption for built-up streets; review industrial fill and raised approaches separately.
workingStandard: The author considers the initial supported holdout errors (about 0.23 m ground and 0.25 m streets) close to the required accuracy. Use this as a first-pass baseline; prioritise sparse coverage, large discrepancies and consequential bank/structure/flow-path joins over marginal residual improvements.
floodInterpretation: The author accepts about 30 cm as a useful working terrain accuracy target because historical high-water levels and other flood inputs are imprecise. The reported 23–25 cm holdout errors are averages on supported predictions, not a universal 30 cm error bound. Evaluate plausible water-level ranges against broad historical flood extent and flow routes; prioritise consequential barriers and connections rather than an exact inundation outline. Regional hydraulic calibration remains unfinished.

targetedMapChecks.finding: Full mosaic and 8x crop inspected. The 3.4 figure and separate dot above it lie within the lane, beside the L of LANE. No bank hatching surrounds this dot. Nearby lane readings are also low, while some streets to the north are higher.
targetedMapChecks.decision: Retain the existing 3.4 ft road observation. Its approximately +2.15 m holdout prediction error is a warning about smoothing over local relief, not a reason to raise or reject the observed lane. No adjoining marsh height or fill thickness is established by this dot.

targetedMapChecks.surface: Campbell Road beside the railway cutting, south of the bridge
targetedMapChecks.finding: Full mosaic, 8x dot crop and 3x context inspected. 44.9 is clear and its dot lies in Campbell Road beside the railway cutting, south of the bridge. Nearby bridge-area readings reach 45.0 ft; adjoining roads are lower. This is a real recorded local high point, not a digit error. The map does not by itself quantify natural relief versus made ground.
targetedMapChecks.decision: Retain 44.9 ft as a road-surface constraint. Its roughly -2.19 m held-out prediction discrepancy flags the need to preserve local street profiles and railway-cutting geometry. Do not lower it to neighbouring street averages or extend the road level onto the railway floor.

Retain the clear 16.4 ft White Post Lane dot. The map places it east of the railway beside the chemical works; the large held-out prediction draws on sparse surrounding controls across strong local relief. Do not raise the observed lane to a neighbouring average.

Retain the clear 42.5 ft park-path dot beside St Augustine’s church. It is distinct from the church building and lower 39.6 ft church-ground dot. Reconcile the local park-edge slope when joining terrain; do not infer a reading error from the holdout residual.

Retain the clear 40.9 ft Cassland Road dot. The figure is printed on the park side, but its survey dot is in the roadway to the east. Preserve this position and local road profile when reconciling the park margin and railway cutting.

limitations: 500 m is an experimental spacing limit, not established accuracy.
Linear triangles have continuous heights along shared edges but discontinuous slopes.
Water geometry constrains interpolation; road/rail earthworks and other dry-land barriers still need reconciliation.
Marsh lane and developed street levels are retained without an invented fill correction; adjoining ground differences remain uncertain.
Blank regions are unsupported, not flat ground. Surface-domain edges are not physical banks.
Reviewed display patches and detailed core remain unchanged; this trial does not replace them.
Holdout residuals test internal consistency; they do not validate datum, date, fill thickness or historical accuracy.
